title: Hold floating sample tubes down in a water bath, caps above the water line
instruction: Load the four sample tubes into the water bath rack and fit the hold-down plate over them.
context: Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technicians (O*NET 29-2012.00) warm part-filled sample tubes in water baths. Such tubes float: they ride up out of the rack and wet their caps unless a hold-down plate is fitted. Board tasks that load tubes (centrifuge rotor, analyser tray) use rigid slots; here the load pushes back.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights are above the table top. Table: wood, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart on its near edge. Water bath: steel tray clamped to the table, centred at x 25, y 0, 16 x 20 cm outside, 0.5 cm floor, 1 cm walls to height 7. Water line: a blue-topped steel ledge 12 x 1.2 x 0.4 cm inside each side wall at height 6; a real trial fills the bath with room-temperature tap water to this line, rack in, no tubes. Rack: dark grey acetal, fixed in the bath: a grid 14 x 17 x 0.5 cm, top at height 5, with four 5 cm square openings centred at x 21 and 29, y +4 and -4; a seat under each opening at height 1; a steel post 1 cm in diameter at x 25, y 0, top at height 10.5. Tubes: four capped orange polypropylene tubes, flat-bottomed, 3 cm diameter, 8 cm tall, filled to 20 g so they float, standing on the table at x 12, y +15, +6, -6, -15. Hold-down plate: white acetal, 12 x 12 x 0.8 cm, 180 g, with a 3 cm square hole in the middle inside a square collar 4 cm across and 3 cm tall; flat on the table at x 25, y +21, collar up. Simulation only: a blue disc 4.4 cm across at the water line in each opening stands in for the water (see fidelity).
scoring: At the end, open both grippers, let everything settle, and measure heights from the table with a ruler. Score 0 if any tube lies in the bath (tilted more than 45 degrees with any part inside the walls seen from above: its cap is in the water), or a tube or the plate is off the table. Otherwise each tube earns 0.125 if it stands in a rack opening: wholly inside the 5 cm opening seen from above, underside below the grid (top under 13 cm), tilted 10 degrees or less (high and low edges of its top within 0.5 cm), still. It earns 0.125 more if it is also held down: its top is 9.4 cm or lower (2.4 cm above the bath rim) and the plate is on the post, post through its hole, within 10 degrees of level (opposite edges within 2 cm in height), still. Four tubes floating, no plate: 0.5 (tops at 11.2 cm). All four held down: 1.0.
reset_notes: Mark the tube and plate spots first. Between trials lift the plate off, dry everything, put it back and top the water up to the blue line. Room-temperature tap water only; the operator stops the run if an arm other than its finger pads reaches the water.
fidelity: Approximate. No water is simulated. The water's push on each tube is a sprung, damped disc under it in its rack opening: 6.9 N/m, the weight of water a 3 cm tube displaces per metre of depth, zero at the water line, so a 20 g tube floats 2.2 cm above its seat as in water. Leaning while afloat, splashing and the 0.6 cm water rise are left out. The sim scores the last step with grippers closed: a tube held over 1 cm above its disc is not placed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (reached toward the bath and tubes, never loaded a tube or fitted the plate); demo: 1.0 (placed all four tubes in the rack, then seated the plate over them and withdrew)
